validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in one-carbon metabolism and trans-sulfuration pathway genes and susceptibility to bladder cancer.
validated_results.reason: The reported analyses concern single nucleotide polymorphisms in one-carbon metabolism genes and gene-gene interaction, with no population-wide folate/folic acid intake estimate for bladder cancer risk in this paper.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in one-carbon metabolism and trans-sulfuration pathway genes and susceptibility to bladder cancer.
validated_results.reason: Glutathione appears only as the metabolic product of CTH/GSTM1 genotypes studied, and no population-wide glutathione exposure estimate for bladder cancer incidence is reported.

validated_results.title: The investigation of GSTT1, GSTM1 and SOD polymorphism in bladder cancer patients.
validated_results.reason: The study evaluates GSTT1, GSTM1 and MnSOD genotype frequencies rather than any nutritional glutathione exposure, so no population-wide exposure estimate exists.

validated_results.title: The green tea compound, (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate downregulates N-cadherin and suppresses migration of bladder carcinoma cells.
validated_results.reason: Evidence comes exclusively from human bladder carcinoma cell lines and mouse xenograft experiments with EGCG, with no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: The green tea compound, (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate downregulates N-cadherin and suppresses migration of bladder carcinoma cells.
validated_results.reason: The tea compound EGCG is tested only in cultured bladder carcinoma cells and mouse xenografts, so no human cancer incidence is assessed.

validated_results.title: Association of vitamin-D receptor (Fok-I) gene polymorphism with bladder cancer in an Indian population.
validated_results.reason: The case-control analysis addresses vitamin-D receptor Fok-I/Taq-I genotypes and haplotypes rather than vitamin D intake or status, providing no population-wide nutritional exposure estimate.

validated_results.title: The role of glutathione transferases M1 and T1 in individual susceptibility to bladder cancer in a Tunisian population.
validated_results.reason: The exposure examined is GSTM1/GSTT1 null genotype rather than nutritional glutathione, so no population-wide glutathione exposure estimate is available.

validated_results.title: The role of glutathione transferases M1 and T1 in individual susceptibility to bladder cancer in a Tunisian population.
validated_results.reason: Risk of transitional cell carcinoma is analyzed by glutathione transferase deletion genotypes, not by any measured nutritional glutathione exposure.
